entries.subject: DAMIT 329: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-329.txt. Model 329, version 2011-04-21, pole (224°, -4°), period 10.04008 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 64.37 ± 0.89 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 258 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: AKARI’s thermal diameter sets an approximate mesh volume scale. The inferred shape does not resolve craters or concavities. Published convex inversion from Hanuš (2011). The selected archive solution is retained as a reproducible coarse model. An alternative pole remains possible; no unique orientation is claimed. Alternative archive solutions: model 330, pole ['40', '-9'], [Model 330](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/330) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 330: pole (40°, -9°), 10.04007 h, version 2011-04-21. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
